texts.php.1.12: But I would ye should understand, brethren, that the things which happened to me have fallen out rather to the furtherance of the gospel;
texts.php.1.13: So that my bonds in Christ are manifest in all the palace, and in all other places;
texts.php.1.14: And many of the brethren in the Lord, becoming confident by my bonds, are much more bold to speak the word without fear.
texts.php.1.15: Some indeed preach Christ even from envy and strife; and some also from good will.
texts.php.1.16: The one preach Christ from contention, not sincerely, supposing to add affliction to my bonds:
texts.php.1.17: But the other from love, knowing that I am set for the defense of the gospel.
texts.php.1.18: What then? notwithstanding, every way, whether in pretense or in truth, Christ is preached; and I therein do rejoice, yes, and will rejoice.
texts.php.1.19: For I know that this will turn to my salvation through your prayer, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,
texts.php.1.20: According to my earnest expectation and hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but that with all boldness, as always, so now also, Christ will be magnified in my body, whether by life, or by death.
texts.php.1.21: For to me to live is Christ, and to die is gain.
texts.php.1.22: But if I live in the flesh, this is the fruit of my labor: yet what I shall choose I know not.
texts.php.1.23: For I am in a strait betwixt two, having a desire to depart, and to be with Christ; which is far better:
texts.php.1.24: Nevertheless, to abide in the flesh is more needful for you.
texts.php.1.25: And having this confidence, I know that I shall abide and continue with you all for your furtherance and joy of faith;
texts.php.1.26: That your rejoicing for me may be more abundant in Jesus Christ by my coming to you again.
texts.php.1.27: Only let your manner of life be as it becometh the gospel of Christ: that whether I come and see you, or else be absent, I may hear of your affairs, that ye stand fast in one spirit, with one mind striving together for the faith of the gospel;
texts.php.1.28: And in nothing terrified by your adversaries: which is to them an evident token of perdition, but to you of salvation, and that from God.
texts.php.1.29: For to you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake;
texts.php.1.30: Having the same conflict which ye saw in me, and now hear to be in me.
texts.php.2.1: If there is therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies,
texts.php.2.2: Fulfill ye my joy, that ye be like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.
texts.php.2.3: Let nothing be done through strife or vain glory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
texts.php.2.4: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
texts.php.2.5: Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus:
texts.php.2.6: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:
texts.php.2.7: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:
texts.php.2.8: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient to death, even the death of the cross.
texts.php.2.9: Wherefore God also hath highly exalted him, and given him a name which is above every name:
texts.php.2.10: That at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things on earth, and things under the earth;
texts.php.2.11: And that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
texts.php.2.12: Wherefore, my beloved, as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling.
texts.php.2.13: For it is God who worketh in you both to will and to do of his good pleasure.
texts.php.2.14: Do all things without murmurings and disputings:
texts.php.2.15: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world;
texts.php.2.16: Holding forth the word of life; that I may rejoice in the day of Christ, that I have not run in vain, neither labored in vain.
texts.php.2.17: And if I am even offered upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I joy, and rejoice with you all.
texts.php.2.18: For the same cause also do ye joy, and rejoice with me.
texts.php.2.19: But I trust in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy shortly to you, that I also may be of good comfort, when I know your state.
texts.php.2.20: For I have no man like-minded, who will naturally care for your state.
texts.php.2.21: For all seek their own, not the things of Jesus Christ.
texts.php.2.22: But ye know the proof of him, that as a son with the father, he hath served with me in the gospel.
texts.php.2.23: Him therefore I hope to send presently, so soon as I shall see how it will go with me.
texts.php.2.24: But I trust in the Lord that I also myself shall come shortly.
texts.php.2.25: Yet I supposed it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother, and companion in labor, and fellow-soldier, but your messenger, and he that ministered to my wants.
texts.php.2.26: For he longed after you all, and was full of heaviness, because ye had heard that he was sick.
texts.php.2.27: For indeed he was sick nigh to death: but God had mercy on him; and not on him only, but on me also, lest I should have sorrow upon sorrow.
texts.php.2.28: I sent him therefore the more speedily, that, when ye see him again, ye may rejoice, and that I may be the less sorrowful.
texts.php.2.29: Receive him therefore in the Lord with all gladness; and hold such in reputation:
texts.php.2.30: Because for the work of Christ he was nigh to death, not regarding his life, to supply the want of your service towards me.
texts.php.3.1: Finally, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord. To write the same things to you, to me indeed is not grievous, but for you it is safe.
texts.php.3.2: Beware of dogs, beware of evil-workers, beware of the concision.
texts.php.3.3: For we are the circumcision, who worship God in the spirit, and rejoice in Christ Jesus, and have no confidence in the flesh.
texts.php.3.4: Though I might also have confidence in the flesh. If any other man thinketh that he hath reason to trust in the flesh, I more:
texts.php.3.5: Circumcised the eighth day, of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of the Hebrews; with respect to the law, a Pharisee;
texts.php.3.6: Concerning zeal, persecuting the church; with respect to the righteousness which is by the law, blameless.
texts.php.3.7: But what things were gain to me, those I counted loss for Christ.
texts.php.3.8: Yes doubtless, and I count all things to be loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and do count them to be dung, that I may win Christ,
texts.php.3.9: And be found in him, not having my own righteousness, which is from the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith:
texts.php.3.10: That I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being made conformable to his death;
texts.php.3.11: If by any means I may attain to the resurrection of the dead.
texts.php.3.12: Not as though I had already attained, either were already perfect: but I pursue, if that I may apprehend that for which also I am apprehended by Christ Jesus.
texts.php.3.13: Brethren, I count not myself to have apprehended: but this one thing I do, forgetting those things which are behind, and reaching forward to those things which are before,
texts.php.3.14: I press towards the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.3.15: Let us therefore, as many as are perfect, be thus minded: and if in any thing ye are otherwise minded, God will reveal even this to you.
texts.php.3.16: Nevertheless, to what we have already attained, let us walk by the same rule, let us mind the same thing.
texts.php.3.17: Brethren, be followers together of me, and mark them who walk so as ye have us for an example.
texts.php.3.18: (For many walk, of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they are the enemies of the cross of Christ:
texts.php.3.19: Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.)
texts.php.3.20: For our conversation is in heaven; from whence also we look for the Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ:
texts.php.3.21: Who will change our vile body, that it may be fashioned like to his glorious body, according to the working by which he is able even to subdue all things to himself.
texts.php.4.1: Therefore, my brethren dearly beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand fast in the Lord, my dearly beloved.
texts.php.4.2: I beseech Euodias, and beseech Syntyche, that they be of the same mind in the Lord.
texts.php.4.3: And I entreat thee also, true yoke-fellow, help those women who labored with me in the gospel, with Clement also, and with other my fellow-laborers, whose names are in the book of life.
texts.php.4.4: Rejoice in the Lord always: and again I say, Rejoice.
texts.php.4.5: Let your moderation be known to all men. The Lord is at hand.
texts.php.4.6: Be anxious for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known to God.
texts.php.4.7: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, will keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
texts.php.4.8: Finally, brethren, whatever things are true, whatever things are honest, whatever things are just, whatever things are pure, whatever things are lovely, whatever things are of good report; if there is any virtue, and if there is any praise, think on these things.
texts.php.4.9: Those things, which ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, do: and the God of peace will be with you.
texts.php.4.10: But I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at the last your care of me hath flourished again; wherein ye were also careful, but ye lacked opportunity.
texts.php.4.11: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatever state I am, with that to be content.
texts.php.4.12: I know both how to be abased, and I know how to abound: every where and in all things I am instructed both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need.
texts.php.4.13: I can do all things through Christ who strengtheneth me.
texts.php.4.14: Notwithstanding ye have done well, that ye did communicate with my affliction.
texts.php.4.15: Now, ye Philippians, know also, that in the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church communicated with me as concerning giving and receiving, but ye only.
texts.php.4.16: For even in Thessalonica ye sent once and again to my necessity.
texts.php.4.17: Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account.
texts.php.4.18: But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received from Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odor of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God.
texts.php.4.19: But my God will supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
texts.php.4.20: Now to God and our Father be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
texts.php.4.21: Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren who are with me greet you.
texts.php.4.22: All the saints salute you, chiefly they that are of Cesar's household.
texts.php.4.23: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

texts.php.1.1: Paul and Timotheus, bondmen of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with [the] overseers and ministers;
texts.php.1.2: grace to you, and peace from God our Father and [the] Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.php.1.3: I thank my God for my whole remembrance of you,
texts.php.1.4: constantly in my every supplication, making the supplication for you all with joy,
texts.php.1.5: because of your fellowship with the gospel, from the first day until now;
texts.php.1.6: having confidence of this very thing, that he who has begun in you a good work will complete it unto Jesus Christ's day:
texts.php.1.7: as it is righteous for me to think this as to you all, because ye have *me* in your hearts, and that both in my bonds and in the defence and confirmation of the glad tidings ye are all participators in my grace.
texts.php.1.8: For God is my witness how I long after you all in [the] bowels of Christ Jesus.
texts.php.1.9: And this I pray, that your love may abound yet more and more in full knowledge and all intelligence,
texts.php.1.10: that ye may judge of and approve the things that are more excellent, in order that ye may be pure and without offence for Christ's day,
texts.php.1.11: being complete as regards the fruit of righteousness, which [is] by Jesus Christ, to God's glory and praise.
texts.php.1.12: But I would have you know, brethren, that the circumstances in which I am have turned out rather to the furtherance of the glad tidings,
texts.php.1.13: so that my bonds have become manifest [as being] in Christ in all the praetorium and to all others;
texts.php.1.14: and that the most of the brethren, trusting in [the] Lord through my bonds, dare more abundantly to speak the word of God fearlessly.
texts.php.1.15: Some indeed also for envy and strife, but some also for good will, preach the Christ.
texts.php.1.16: These indeed out of love, knowing that I am set for the defence of the glad tidings;
texts.php.1.17: but those out of contention, announce the Christ, not purely, supposing to arouse tribulation for my bonds.
texts.php.1.18: What is it then? at any rate, in every way, whether in pretext or in truth, Christ is announced; and in this I rejoice, yea, also I will rejoice;
texts.php.1.19: for I know that this shall turn out for me to salvation, through your supplication and [the] supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ;
texts.php.1.20: according to my earnest expectation and hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, but in all boldness, as always, now also Christ shall be magnified in my body whether by life or by death.
texts.php.1.21: For for me to live [is] Christ, and to die gain;
texts.php.1.22: but if to live in flesh [is my lot], this is for me worth the while: and what I shall choose I cannot tell.
texts.php.1.23: But I am pressed by both, having the desire for departure and being with Christ, [for] [it is] very much better,
texts.php.1.24: but remaining in the flesh [is] more necessary for your sakes;
texts.php.1.25: and having confidence of this, I know that I shall remain and abide along with you all, for your progress and joy in faith;
texts.php.1.26: that your boasting may abound in Christ Jesus through me by my presence again with you.
texts.php.1.27: Only conduct yourselves worthily of the glad tidings of the Christ, in order that whether coming and seeing you, or absent, I may hear of what concerns you, that ye stand firm in one spirit, with one soul, labouring together in the same conflict with the faith of the glad tidings;
texts.php.1.28: and not frightened in anything by the opposers, which is to them a demonstration of destruction, but of your salvation, and that from God;
texts.php.1.29: because to you has been given, as regards Christ, not only the believing on him but the suffering for him also,
texts.php.1.30: having the same conflict which ye have seen in me, and now hear of in me.
texts.php.2.1: If then [there be] any comfort in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of [the] Spirit, if any bowels and compassions,
texts.php.2.2: fulfil my joy, that ye may think the same thing, having the same love, joined in soul, thinking one thing;
texts.php.2.3: [let] nothing [be] in the spirit of strife or vain glory, but, in lowliness of mind, each esteeming the other as more excellent than themselves;
texts.php.2.4: regarding not each his own [qualities], but each those of others also.
texts.php.2.5: For let this mind be in you which [was] also in Christ Jesus;
texts.php.2.6: who, subsisting in the form of God, did not esteem it an object of rapine to be on an equality with God;
texts.php.2.7: but emptied himself, taking a bondman's form, taking his place in [the] likeness of men;
texts.php.2.8: and having been found in figure as a man, humbled himself, becoming obedient even unto death, and [that the] death of [the] cross.
texts.php.2.9: Wherefore also God highly exalted him, and granted him a name, that which is above every name,
texts.php.2.10: that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow, of heavenly and earthly and infernal [beings],
texts.php.2.11: and every tongue confess that Jesus Christ [is] Lord to God [the] Father's glory.
texts.php.2.12: So that, my beloved, even as ye have always obeyed, not as in my presence only, but now much rather in my absence, work out your own salvation with fear and trembling,
texts.php.2.13: for it is God who works in you both the willing and the working according to [his] good pleasure.
texts.php.2.14: Do all things without murmurings and reasonings,
texts.php.2.15: that ye may be harmless and simple, irreproachable children of God in the midst of a crooked and perverted generation; among whom ye appear as lights in [the] world,
texts.php.2.16: holding forth [the] word of life, so as to be a boast for me in Christ's day, that I have not run in vain nor laboured in vain.
texts.php.2.17: But if also I am poured out as a libation on the sacrifice and ministration of your faith, I rejoice, and rejoice in common with you all.
texts.php.2.18: In like manner do *ye* also rejoice, and rejoice with me.
texts.php.2.19: But I hope in [the] Lord Jesus to send Timotheus to you shortly, that *I* also may be refreshed, knowing how ye get on.
texts.php.2.20: For I have no one like-minded who will care with genuine feeling how ye get on.
texts.php.2.21: For all seek their own things, not the things of Jesus Christ.
texts.php.2.22: But ye know the proof of him, that, as a child a father, he has served with me in the work of the glad tidings.
texts.php.2.23: Him therefore I hope to send immediately, as soon as I shall see how it goes with me:
texts.php.2.24: but I trust in [the] Lord that I myself also shall soon come;
texts.php.2.25: but I have thought it necessary to send to you Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow-workman and fellow-soldier, but your messenger and minister to my need,
texts.php.2.26: since he had a longing desire after you all, and was distressed because ye had heard that he was sick;
texts.php.2.27: for he was also sick close to death, but God had mercy on him, and not indeed on him alone, but also on me, that I might not have sorrow upon sorrow.
texts.php.2.28: I have sent him therefore the more diligently, that seeing him ye might again rejoice, and that *I* might be the less sorrowful.
texts.php.2.29: Receive him therefore in [the] Lord with all joy, and hold such in honour;
texts.php.2.30: because for the sake of the work he drew near even to death, venturing his life that he might fill up what lacked in your ministration toward me.
texts.php.3.1: For the rest, my brethren, rejoice in [the] Lord: to write the same things to you, to me [is] not irksome, and for you safe.
texts.php.3.2: See to dogs, see to evil workmen, see to the concision.
texts.php.3.3: For *we* are the circumcision, who worship by [the] Spirit of God, and boast in Christ Jesus, and do not trust in flesh.
texts.php.3.4: Though *I* have [my] trust even in flesh; if any other think to trust in flesh, *I* rather:
texts.php.3.5: as to circumcision, [I received it] the eighth day; of [the] race of Israel, of [the] tribe of Benjamin, Hebrew of Hebrews; as to [the] law, a Pharisee;
texts.php.3.6: as to zeal, persecuting the assembly; as to righteousness which [is] in [the] law, found blameless;
texts.php.3.7: but what things were gain to me these I counted, on account of Christ, loss.
texts.php.3.8: But surely I count also all things to be loss on account of the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, on account of whom I have suffered the loss of all, and count them to be filth, that I may gain Christ;
texts.php.3.9: and that I may be found in him, not having my righteousness, which [would be] on the principle of law, but that which is by faith of Christ, the righteousness which [is] of God through faith,
texts.php.3.10: to know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being conformed to his death,
texts.php.3.11: if any way I arrive at the resurrection from among [the] dead.
texts.php.3.12: Not that I have already obtained [the prize], or am already perfected; but I pursue, if also I may get possession [of it], seeing that also I have been taken possession of by Christ [Jesus].
texts.php.3.13: Brethren, *I* do not count to have got possession myself; but one thing -- forgetting the things behind, and stretching out to the things before,
texts.php.3.14: I pursue, [looking] towards [the] goal, for the prize of the calling on high of God in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.3.15: As many therefore as [are] perfect, let us be thus minded; and if ye are any otherwise minded, this also God shall reveal to you.
texts.php.3.16: But whereto we have attained, [let us] walk in the same steps.
texts.php.3.17: Be imitators [all] together of me, brethren, and fix your eyes on those walking thus as you have us for a model;
texts.php.3.18: (for many walk of whom I have told you often, and now tell you even weeping, that they [are] the enemies of the cross of Christ:
texts.php.3.19: whose end [is] destruction, whose god [is] the belly, and [their] glory in their shame, who mind earthly things:)
texts.php.3.20: for *our* commonwealth has its existence in [the] heavens, from which also we await the Lord Jesus Christ [as] Saviour,
texts.php.3.21: who shall transform our body of humiliation into conformity to his body of glory, according to the working of [the] power which he has even to subdue all things to himself.
texts.php.4.1: So that, my brethren, beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, thus stand fast in [the] Lord, beloved.
texts.php.4.2: I exhort Euodia, and exhort Syntyche, to be of the same mind in [the] Lord;
texts.php.4.3: yea, I ask thee also, true yokefellow, assist them, who have contended along with me in the glad tidings, with Clement also, and my other fellow-labourers, whose names [are] in [the] book of life.
texts.php.4.4: Rejoice in [the] Lord always: again I will say, Rejoice.
texts.php.4.5: Let your gentleness be known of all men. The Lord [is] near.
texts.php.4.6: Be careful about nothing; but in everything, by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God;
texts.php.4.7: and the peace of God, which surpasses every understanding, shall guard your hearts and your thoughts by Christ Jesus.
texts.php.4.8: For the rest, brethren, whatsoever things [are] true, whatsoever things [are] noble, whatsoever things [are] just, whatsoever things [are] pure, whatsoever things [are] amiable, whatsoever things [are] of good report; if [there be] any virtue and if any praise, think on these things.
texts.php.4.9: What ye have both learned, and received, and heard, and seen in me, these things do; and the God of peace shall be with you.
texts.php.4.10: But I rejoiced in [the] Lord greatly, that now however at length ye have revived your thinking of me, though surely ye did also think [of me], but lacked opportunity.
texts.php.4.11: Not that I speak as regards privation, for as to me *I* have learnt in those circumstances in which I am, to be satisfied in myself.
texts.php.4.12: I know both how to be abased and I know how to abound. In everything and in all things I am initiated both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer privation.
texts.php.4.13: I have strength for all things in him that gives me power.
texts.php.4.14: But ye have done well in taking part in my affliction.
texts.php.4.15: And know also *ye*, O Philippians, that in [the] beginning of the gospel, when I came out of Macedonia, no assembly communicated [anything] to me in [the] way of giving and receiving save *ye* alone;
texts.php.4.16: for also in Thessalonica once and even twice ye sent to me for my need.
texts.php.4.17: Not that I seek gift, but I seek fruit abounding to your account.
texts.php.4.18: But I have all things in full supply and abound; I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things [sent] from you, an odour of sweet savour, an acceptable sacrifice, agreeable to God.
texts.php.4.19: But my God shall abundantly supply all your need according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.4.20: But to our God and Father [be] glory to the ages of ages. Amen.
texts.php.4.21: Salute every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren who [are] with me salute you.
texts.php.4.22: All the saints salute you, and specially those of the household of Caesar.
texts.php.4.23: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ [be] with your spirit. Amen.

texts.php.1.1: Paul and Timotheus, servants of Jesus Christ, to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with overseers and ministrants;
texts.php.1.2: Grace to you, and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.php.1.3: I give thanks to my God upon all the remembrance of you,
texts.php.1.4: always, in every supplication of mine for you all, with joy making the supplication,
texts.php.1.5: for your contribution to the good news from the first day till now,
texts.php.1.6: having been confident of this very thing, that He who did begin in you a good work, will perform [it] till a day of Jesus Christ,
texts.php.1.7: according as it is righteous for me to think this in behalf of you all, because of my having you in the heart, both in my bonds, and [in] the defence and confirmation of the good news, all of you being fellow-partakers with me of grace.
texts.php.1.8: For God is my witness, how I long for you all in the bowels of Jesus Christ,
texts.php.1.9: and this I pray, that your love yet more and more may abound in full knowledge, and all judgment,
texts.php.1.10: for your proving the things that differ, that ye may be pure and offenceless -- to a day of Christ,
texts.php.1.11: being filled with the fruit of righteousness, that [is] through Jesus Christ, to the glory and praise of God.
texts.php.1.12: And I wish you to know, brethren, that the things concerning me, rather to an advancement of the good news have come,
texts.php.1.13: so that my bonds have become manifest in Christ in the whole praetorium, and to the other places -- all,
texts.php.1.14: and the greater part of the brethren in the Lord, having confidence by my bonds, are more abundantly bold -- fearlessly to speak the word.
texts.php.1.15: Certain, indeed, even through envy and contention, and certain also through good-will, do preach the Christ;
texts.php.1.16: the one, indeed, of rivalry the Christ do proclaim, not purely, supposing to add affliction to my bonds,
texts.php.1.17: and the other out of love, having known that for defence of the good news I am set:
texts.php.1.18: what then? in every way, whether in pretence or in truth, Christ is proclaimed -- and in this I rejoice, yea, and shall rejoice.
texts.php.1.19: For I have known that this shall fall out to me for salvation, through your supplication, and the supply of the Spirit of Christ Jesus,
texts.php.1.20: according to my earnest expectation and hope, that in nothing I shall be ashamed, and in all freedom, as always, also now Christ shall be magnified in my body, whether through life or through death,
texts.php.1.21: for to me to live [is] Christ, and to die gain.
texts.php.1.22: And if to live in the flesh [is] to me a fruit of work, then what shall I choose? I know not;
texts.php.1.23: for I am pressed by the two, having the desire to depart, and to be with Christ, for it is far better,
texts.php.1.24: and to remain in the flesh is more necessary on your account,
texts.php.1.25: and of this being persuaded, I have known that I shall remain and continue with you all, to your advancement and joy of the faith,
texts.php.1.26: that your boasting may abound in Christ Jesus in me through my presence again to you.
texts.php.1.27: Only worthily of the good news of the Christ conduct ye yourselves, that, whether having come and seen you, whether being absent I may hear of the things concerning you, that ye stand fast in one spirit, with one soul, striving together for the faith of the good news,
texts.php.1.28: and not terrified in anything by those opposing, which to them indeed is a token of destruction, and to you of salvation, and that from God;
texts.php.1.29: because to you it was granted, on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also on behalf of him to suffer;
texts.php.1.30: the same conflict having, such as ye saw in me, and now hear of in me.
texts.php.2.1: If, then, any exhortation [is] in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of spirit, if any bowels and mercies,
texts.php.2.2: fulfil ye my joy, that ye may mind the same thing -- having the same love -- of one soul -- minding the one thing,
texts.php.2.3: nothing in rivalry or vain-glory, but in humility of mind one another counting more excellent than yourselves --
texts.php.2.4: each not to your own look ye, but each also to the things of others.
texts.php.2.5: For, let this mind be in you that [is] also in Christ Jesus,
texts.php.2.6: who, being in the form of God, thought [it] not robbery to be equal to God,
texts.php.2.7: but did empty himself, the form of a servant having taken, in the likeness of men having been made,
texts.php.2.8: and in fashion having been found as a man, he humbled himself, having become obedient unto death -- death even of a cross,
texts.php.2.9: wherefore, also, God did highly exalt him, and gave to him a name that [is] above every name,
texts.php.2.10: that in the name of Jesus every knee may bow -- of heavenlies, and earthlies, and what are under the earth --
texts.php.2.11: and every tongue may confess that Jesus Christ [is] Lord, to the glory of God the Father.
texts.php.2.12: So that, my beloved, as ye always obey, not as in my presence only, but now much more in my absence, with fear and trembling your own salvation work out,
texts.php.2.13: for God it is who is working in you both to will and to work for His good pleasure.
texts.php.2.14: All things do without murmurings and reasonings,
texts.php.2.15: that ye may become blameless and harmless, children of God, unblemished in the midst of a generation crooked and perverse, among whom ye do appear as luminaries in the world,
texts.php.2.16: the word of life holding forth, for rejoicing to me in regard to a day of Christ, that not in vain did I run, nor in vain did I labour;
texts.php.2.17: but if also I am poured forth upon the sacrifice and service of your faith, I rejoice and joy with you all,
texts.php.2.18: because of this do ye also rejoice and joy with me.
texts.php.2.19: And I hope, in the Lord Jesus, Timotheus to send quickly to you, that I also may be of good spirit, having known the things concerning you,
texts.php.2.20: for I have no one like-minded, who sincerely for the things concerning you will care,
texts.php.2.21: for the whole seek their own things, not the things of the Christ Jesus,
texts.php.2.22: and the proof of him ye know, that as a child [serveth] a father, with me he did serve in regard to the good news;
texts.php.2.23: him, indeed, therefore, I hope to send, when I may see through the things concerning me -- immediately;
texts.php.2.24: and I trust in the Lord that I myself also shall quickly come.
texts.php.2.25: And I thought [it] necessary Epaphroditus -- my brother, and fellow-workman, and fellow-soldier, and your apostle and servant to my need -- to send unto you,
texts.php.2.26: seeing he was longing after you all, and in heaviness, because ye heard that he ailed,
texts.php.2.27: for he also ailed nigh to death, but God did deal kindly with him, and not with him only, but also with me, that sorrow upon sorrow I might not have.
texts.php.2.28: The more eagerly, therefore, I did send him, that having seen him again ye may rejoice, and I may be the less sorrowful;
texts.php.2.29: receive him, therefore, in the Lord, with all joy, and hold such in honour,
texts.php.2.30: because on account of the work of the Christ he drew near to death, having hazarded the life that he might fill up your deficiency of service unto me.
texts.php.3.1: As to the rest, my brethren, rejoice in the Lord; the same things to write to you to me indeed is not tiresome, and for you [is] sure;
texts.php.3.2: look to the dogs, look to the evil-workers, look to the concision;
texts.php.3.3: for we are the circumcision, who by the Spirit are serving God, and glorying in Christ Jesus, and in flesh having no trust,
texts.php.3.4: though I also have [cause of] trust in flesh. If any other one doth think to have trust in flesh, I more;
texts.php.3.5: circumcision on the eighth day! of the race of Israel! of the tribe of Benjamin! a Hebrew of Hebrews! according to law a Pharisee!
texts.php.3.6: according to zeal persecuting the assembly! according to righteousness that is in law becoming blameless!
texts.php.3.7: But what things were to me gains, these I have counted, because of the Christ, loss;
texts.php.3.8: yes, indeed, and I count all things to be loss, because of the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, because of whom of the all things I suffered loss, and do count them to be refuse, that Christ I may gain, and be found in him,
texts.php.3.9: not having my righteousness, which [is] of law, but that which [is] through faith of Christ -- the righteousness that is of God by the faith,
texts.php.3.10: to know him, and the power of his rising again, and the fellowship of his sufferings, being conformed to his death,
texts.php.3.11: if anyhow I may attain to the rising again of the dead.
texts.php.3.12: Not that I did already obtain, or have been already perfected; but I pursue, if also I may lay hold of that for which also I was laid hold of by the Christ Jesus;
texts.php.3.13: brethren, I do not reckon myself to have laid hold; and one thing -- the things behind indeed forgetting, and to the things before stretching forth --
texts.php.3.14: to the mark I pursue for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.3.15: As many, therefore, as [are] perfect -- let us think this, and if [in] anything ye think otherwise, this also shall God reveal to you,
texts.php.3.16: but to what we have come -- by the same rule walk, the same thing think;
texts.php.3.17: become followers together of me, brethren, and observe those thus walking, according as ye have us -- a pattern;
texts.php.3.18: for many walk of whom many times I told you -- and now also weeping tell -- the enemies of the cross of the Christ!
texts.php.3.19: whose end [is] destruction, whose god [is] the belly, and whose glory [is] in their shame, who the things on earth are minding.
texts.php.3.20: For our citizenship is in the heavens, whence also a Saviour we await -- the Lord Jesus Christ --
texts.php.3.21: who shall transform the body of our humiliation to its becoming conformed to the body of his glory, according to the working of his power, even to subject to himself the all things.
texts.php.4.1: So then, my brethren, beloved and longed for, my joy and crown, so stand ye in the Lord, beloved.
texts.php.4.2: Euodia I exhort, and Syntyche I exhort, to be of the same mind in the Lord;
texts.php.4.3: and I ask also thee, genuine yoke-fellow, be assisting those women who in the good news did strive along with me, with Clement also, and the others, my fellow-workers, whose names [are] in the book of life.
texts.php.4.4: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, rejoice;
texts.php.4.5: let your forbearance be known to all men; the Lord [is] near;
texts.php.4.6: for nothing be anxious, but in everything by prayer, and by supplication, with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known unto God;
texts.php.4.7: and the peace of God, that is surpassing all understanding, shall guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.4.8: As to the rest, brethren, as many things as are true, as many as [are] grave, as many as [are] righteous, as many as [are] pure, as many as [are] lovely, as many as [are] of good report, if any worthiness, and if any praise, these things think upon;
texts.php.4.9: the things that also ye did learn, and receive, and hear, and saw in me, those do, and the God of the peace shall be with you.
texts.php.4.10: And I rejoiced in the Lord greatly, that now at length ye flourished again in caring for me, for which also ye were caring, and lacked opportunity;
texts.php.4.11: not that in respect of want I say [it], for I did learn in the things in which I am -- to be content;
texts.php.4.12: I have known both to be abased, and I have known to abound; in everything and in all things I have been initiated, both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in want.
texts.php.4.13: For all things I have strength, in Christ's strengthening me;
texts.php.4.14: but ye did well, having communicated with my tribulation;
texts.php.4.15: and ye have known, even ye Philippians, that in the beginning of the good news when I went forth from Macedonia, no assembly did communicate with me in regard to giving and receiving except ye only;
texts.php.4.16: because also in Thessalonica, both once and again to my need ye sent;
texts.php.4.17: not that I seek after the gift, but I seek after the fruit that is overflowing to your account;
texts.php.4.18: and I have all things, and abound; I am filled, having received from Epaphroditus the things from you -- an odour of a sweet smell -- a sacrifice acceptable, well-pleasing to God:
texts.php.4.19: and my God shall supply all your need, according to His riches in glory in Christ Jesus;
texts.php.4.20: and to God, even our Father, [is] the glory -- to the ages of the ages. Amen.
texts.php.4.21: Salute ye every saint in Christ Jesus; there salute you the brethren with me;
texts.php.4.22: there salute you all the saints, and specially those of Caesar's house;
texts.php.4.23: the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ [is] with you all. Amen.

texts.php.1.1: Pablo y Timoteo, siervos de Jesu Cristo, a todos los santos en Cristo Jesús, que están en Filipos, con los obispos, y diáconos:
texts.php.1.2: Gracia a vosotros, y paz de Dios nuestro Padre, y del Señor Jesu Cristo.
texts.php.1.3: Doy gracias a mi Dios, toda vez que me acuerdo de vosotros,
texts.php.1.4: Siempre en todas mis oraciones haciendo oración por todos vosotros con gozo,
texts.php.1.5: De vuestra participación en el evangelio, desde el primer día hasta ahora:
texts.php.1.6: Confiando de esto mismo, es a saber, que el que comenzó en vosotros la buena obra, la perfeccionará hasta el día de Jesu Cristo:
texts.php.1.7: Así como es justo que yo piense esto de todos vosotros, por cuanto os tengo en el corazón; puesto que así en mis prisiones, como en la defensa y confirmación del evangelio, todos vosotros sois partícipes de mi gracia.
texts.php.1.8: Porque testigo me es Dios de como os amo a todos vosotros en las entrañas de Jesu Cristo.
texts.php.1.9: Y esto pido a Dios: Que vuestro amor abunde aun más y más en ciencia y en todo conocimiento:
texts.php.1.10: Para que aprobéis lo mejor, a fin de que seáis sinceros y sin ofensa para el día de Cristo:
texts.php.1.11: Llenos de los frutos de justicia que son por Jesu Cristo, para gloria y loor de Dios.
texts.php.1.12: Mas quiero, hermanos, que sepáis, que las cosas concernientes a mí han contribuido más bien al adelantamiento del evangelio;
texts.php.1.13: De tal manera, que mis prisiones en Cristo se han hecho bien conocidas en todo el palacio, y en todos los demás lugares;
texts.php.1.14: Y los más de los hermanos en el Señor, tomando ánimo con mis prisiones, osan más atrevidamente hablar la palabra sin temor.
texts.php.1.15: Algunos, a la verdad, aun por envidia y porfía predican a Cristo; mas otros también de buena voluntad:
texts.php.1.16: Aquellos por contención anuncian a Cristo, no sinceramente, pensando añadir mayor apretura a mis prisiones:
texts.php.1.17: Mas estos por amor, sabiendo que yo he sido puesto por defensa del evangelio.
texts.php.1.18: ¿Qué hay pues? Esto no obstante, de todas maneras, o por pretexto o por verdad, Cristo es anunciado; y en esto me huelgo, y aun me holgaré.
texts.php.1.19: Porque sé que esto se me tornará a salud por vuestra oración, y por el suplimiento del Espíritu de Jesu Cristo.
texts.php.1.20: Conforme a mi deseo y esperanza, que en nada seré confundido; antes que con toda confianza, como siempre, así ahora también será engrandecido Cristo en mi cuerpo, o por vida, o por muerte.
texts.php.1.21: Porque para mí el vivir es Cristo, y el morir es ganancia.
texts.php.1.22: Mas, si viviere en la carne, esto me da fruto de trabajo; sin embargo lo que escogeré, yo no lo sé;
texts.php.1.23: Porque por ambas partes estoy puesto en estrecho, teniendo deseo de partir, y estar con Cristo, que es mucho mejor:
texts.php.1.24: Mas el quedar en la carne, es más necesario por causa de vosotros.
texts.php.1.25: Y confiando en esto, sé que quedaré, y permaneceré con todos vosotros, para vuestro provecho, y gozo en la fe.
texts.php.1.26: Para que abunde más en Jesu Cristo el motivo de vuestra gloria en mí, por mi venida otra vez a vosotros.
texts.php.1.27: Solamente que vuestro proceder sea digno del evangelio de Cristo; para que, o sea que venga y os vea, o que esté ausente, oiga de vosotros, que estáis firmes en un mismo espíritu, con un mismo ánimo combatiendo juntamente por la fe del evangelio;
texts.php.1.28: Y en nada espantados de los que se oponen, lo cual para ellos ciertamente es indicio de perdición, mas para vosotros de salud, y esto de Dios.
texts.php.1.29: Porque a vosotros os es concedido en nombre de Cristo no solo que creáis en él, sino también que padezcáis por él.
texts.php.1.30: Teniendo en vosotros la misma lucha que habéis visto en mí, y ahora oís estar en mí.
texts.php.2.1: Por tanto, si hay en vosotros alguna consolación en Cristo, si algún refrigerio de amor, si alguna comunión del Espíritu, si algunas entrañas y conmiseraciones,
texts.php.2.2: Cumplíd mi gozo en que penséis lo mismo, teniendo un mismo amor, siendo unánimes, sintiendo una misma cosa.
texts.php.2.3: Nada hagáis por contienda, o por vana gloria; antes en humildad de espíritu, estimándoos inferiores los unos a los otros,
texts.php.2.4: No mirando cada uno a lo que es suyo, mas también a lo que es de los otros.
texts.php.2.5: Haya en vosotros los mismos sentimientos que hubo también en Cristo Jesús:
texts.php.2.6: El cual siendo en forma de Dios, no tuvo por rapiña ser igual a Dios;
texts.php.2.7: Mas se despojó a sí mismo, tomando forma de siervo, hecho a semejanza de los hombres;
texts.php.2.8: Y hallado en su condición como hombre, se humilló a sí mismo, haciéndose obediente hasta la muerte, y muerte de cruz.
texts.php.2.9: Y por lo cual Dios también le ensalzó soberanamente, y le dio nombre que es sobre todo nombre;
texts.php.2.10: Para que al nombre de Jesús toda rodilla de lo celestial, de lo terrenal, y de lo infernal se doble;
texts.php.2.11: Y que toda lengua confiese, que Jesu Cristo es Señor para la gloria de Dios el Padre.
texts.php.2.12: Por tanto, amados míos, como siempre habéis obedecido, no como en mi presencia solamente, mas aun mucho más ahora en mi ausencia, obrád vuestra propia salud con temor y temblor.
texts.php.2.13: Porque Dios es el que en vosotros obra, así el querer como el hacer, según su buena voluntad.
texts.php.2.14: Hacéd todo sin murmuraciones, y sin disputas;
texts.php.2.15: Para que seáis irreprensibles, y sencillos, hijos de Dios, sin culpa, en medio de una raza torcida y perversa, entre los cuales resplandecéis como luminares en el mundo,
texts.php.2.16: Reteniendo la palabra de vida; para que yo pueda gloriarme en el día de Cristo, de que no he corrido en vano, ni trabajado en vano.
texts.php.2.17: Y aunque yo sea sacrificado sobre el sacrificio y servicio de vuestra fe, me huelgo y me regocijo con todos vosotros.
texts.php.2.18: Y por esto mismo holgáos también vosotros, y regocijáos conmigo.
texts.php.2.19: Mas espero en el Señor Jesús, que os enviaré presto a Timoteo, para que yo también esté de buen ánimo, conociendo vuestro estado.
texts.php.2.20: Porque a ninguno tengo tan del mismo ánimo conmigo, que esté sinceramente solícito por vosotros;
texts.php.2.21: Porque todos buscan lo que es suyo propio, no lo que es de Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.2.22: Mas vosotros sabéis la prueba que se ha hecho de él, y es, que como hijo con su padre, él ha servido conmigo en el evangelio.
texts.php.2.23: Así que a éste espero enviaros, luego que viere como van mis negocios.
texts.php.2.24: Mas confío en el Señor que yo mismo también vendré prestamente a vosotros:
texts.php.2.25: Sin embargo tuve por cosa necesaria enviaros a Epafrodito, mi hermano, y compañero, y consiervo mío, mas vuestro mensajero, y el que ministraba a mis necesidades.
texts.php.2.26: Porque tenía deseo vehemente de ver a todos vosotros; y estaba lleno de pesadumbre de que hubieseis oído que había enfermado.
texts.php.2.27: Y cierto que enfermó hasta la muerte; mas Dios tuvo misericordia de él; y no solamente de él mas de mí también, para que yo no tuviese tristeza sobre tristeza.
texts.php.2.28: Así que le envío más presto, para que viéndole otra vez, os regocijéis, y que yo esté con menos tristeza.
texts.php.2.29: Recibídle, pues, en el Señor, con todo regocijo; y tenéd en estima a los tales;
texts.php.2.30: Porque por la obra de Cristo llegó hasta la muerte, exponiendo su vida para suplir vuestra falta en mi servicio.
texts.php.3.1: Resta, hermanos, que os regocijéis en el Señor. Escribiros las mismas cosas, a mí ciertamente no me es gravoso, mas para vosotros es seguro.
texts.php.3.2: Guardáos de los perros, guardáos de los malos obreros, guardáos de la concisión.
texts.php.3.3: Porque nosotros somos la circuncisión, los que servimos en espíritu a Dios, y nos gloriamos en Cristo Jesús, no teniendo confianza en la carne.
texts.php.3.4: Aunque yo tengo también de qué confiar en la carne. Si a alguno le parece que tiene de qué confiar en la carne, yo más que nadie:
texts.php.3.5: Circuncidado al octavo día, del linaje de Israel, de la tribu de Benjamín, Hebreo de Hebreos; en cuanto a la ley, Fariseo;
texts.php.3.6: En cuanto a zelo, perseguidor de la iglesia; en cuanto a la justicia que es en la ley, de vida irreprensible.
texts.php.3.7: Mas aquellas cosas que me eran por ganancia, las tuve por pérdida por amor de Cristo.
texts.php.3.8: Y aun más, que ciertamente todas las cosas tengo por pérdida por la excelencia del conocimiento de Cristo Jesús Señor mío; por amor d el cual lo he perdido todo, y lo tengo por estiércol por ganar a Cristo,
texts.php.3.9: Y ser hallado en él, no teniendo mi propia justicia, que es de la ley, sino la que es por medio de la fe de Cristo, la justicia de Dios por fe:
texts.php.3.10: Por conocerle a él, y a la virtud de su resurrección, y la comunión de sus padecimientos, siendo configurado a su muerte:
texts.php.3.11: Si en alguna manera llegase a la resurrección de los muertos.
texts.php.3.12: No que ya haya alcanzado, ni que ya sea perfecto; mas sigo adelante por si pueda echar mano de aquello, por lo cual Cristo también echó mano de mí.
texts.php.3.13: Hermanos no pienso que yo mismo lo haya alcanzado; empero una cosa hago, y es, que olvidando ciertamente lo que queda atrás, mas extendiéndome a lo que está delante,
texts.php.3.14: Me apresuro hacia el blanco, por el premio de la vocación celestial de Dios en Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.3.15: Así que todos los que somos perfectos, tengamos estos mismos sentimientos; y si en alguna cosa los tenéis diferentes, esto también os revelará Dios.
texts.php.3.16: Empero a lo que hemos ya llegado, vamos por la misma regla, y sintamos una misma cosa.
texts.php.3.17: ¶ Hermanos, sed juntamente imitadores de mí, y mirád los que anduvieren así, como nos tenéis a nosotros por dechado.
texts.php.3.18: (Porque muchos andan, de los cuales os he dicho muchas veces, y ahora también lo digo, aun llorando, que enemigos son de la cruz de Cristo:
texts.php.3.19: Cuyo fin es la perdición: cuyo dios es el vientre, y su gloria es en la confusión de ellos, que piensan solo en lo terreno.)
texts.php.3.20: ¶ Mas nuestra vivienda es en los cielos, de donde también esperamos el Salvador, al Señor Jesu Cristo;
texts.php.3.21: El cual transformará el cuerpo de nuestra bajeza, para que sea hecho semejante a su cuerpo glorificado, según el poder eficiente por el cual puede también sujetar a sí todas las cosas.
texts.php.4.1: Por lo cual, hermanos míos, amados y deseados, mi gozo y mi corona, estád así firmes en el Señor, amados míos.
texts.php.4.2: A Euodias ruego, y ruego a Sintique, que tengan unos mismos sentimientos en el Señor.
texts.php.4.3: Asimismo te ruego también a ti, fiel compañero de yugo, ayuda a aquellas mujeres que combatieron juntamente conmigo por el evangelio, con Clemente también, y los demás mis ayudadores, cuyos nombres están en el libro de la vida:
texts.php.4.4: Regocijáos en el Señor siempre: otra vez digo, que os regocijéis.
texts.php.4.5: Vuestra modestia sea conocida de todos los hombres. El Señor está cerca.
texts.php.4.6: De nada estéis solícitos; sino que en todo dénse a conocer vuestras peticiones delante de Dios por la oración, y el ruego, con hacimiento de gracias.
texts.php.4.7: Y la paz de Dios, que sobrepuja todo entendimiento, guardará vuestros corazones y vuestros entendimientos en Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.4.8: En fin, hermanos, que todo lo que es verdadero, todo lo honesto, todo lo justo, todo lo santo, todo lo amable, todo lo que es de buen nombre: si hay alguna virtud, y si hay alguna alabanza, pensád en las tales cosas.
texts.php.4.9: Lo que aprendisteis, y recibisteis, y oísteis, y visteis en mí, esto hacéd; y el Dios de paz será con vosotros.
texts.php.4.10: ¶ Empero en gran manera me regocijé en el Señor, de que al fin ya reverdecisteis en tener cuidado de mí, de lo cual en verdad estabais solícitos; mas os faltaba la oportunidad.
texts.php.4.11: No es que hablo en cuanto a necesidad; porque yo he aprendido a contentarme con lo que tuviere.
texts.php.4.12: Sé tan bien estar humillado, como sé tener abundancia; donde quiera y en todas cosas soy instruido así para estar harto como para sufrir hambre, lo mismo para tener abundancia como para padecer necesidad:
texts.php.4.13: Todo lo puedo en Cristo que me fortalece.
texts.php.4.14: Todavía, hicisteis bien en que comunicasteis conmigo en mi tribulación.
texts.php.4.15: Ya sabéis también vosotros, oh Filipenses, que al principio del evangelio, cuando me partí de Macedonia, ninguna iglesia comunicó conmigo en materia de dar y de recibir, sino vosotros solos;
texts.php.4.16: Porque aun estando yo en Tesalónica, me enviasteis lo necesario una y dos veces.
texts.php.4.17: No que yo solicite dádivas, mas solicito fruto que abunde para vuestra cuenta.
texts.php.4.18: Empero todo lo tengo, y aun más de lo suficiente: estoy lleno, habiendo recibido de Epafrodito lo que enviasteis, olor de suavidad, sacrificio acepto y agradable a Dios.
texts.php.4.19: Y mi Dios suplirá todo lo que os falta, conforme a sus riquezas, en gloria por Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.4.20: Al Dios, pues, y Padre nuestro sea gloria por siglos de siglos. Amén.
texts.php.4.21: Saludád a todos los santos en Cristo Jesús: os saludan los hermanos que están conmigo.
texts.php.4.22: Os saludan todos los santos; y mayormente los que son de casa de César.
texts.php.4.23: La gracia del Señor nuestro Jesu Cristo sea con todos vosotros. Amén. ¶ Escrita de Roma a los Filipenses por Epafrodito.

texts.php.1.1: Paul and Timothy, servants of Jesus Christ,—unto all the saints in Christ Jesus who are in Philippi, with overseers and ministers:—
texts.php.1.2: Favour unto you, and peace, from God our Father and Lord Jesus Christ.
texts.php.1.3: I am giving thanks unto my God, on occasion of all my remembrance of you,
texts.php.1.4: At all times, in every supplication of mine, in behalf of you all, with joy, my supplication, making,—
texts.php.1.5: On account of your contribution unto the glad-message, from the first day until the present:
texts.php.1.6: Being persuaded of this very thing—that, he who hath begun in you a good work, will perfect it, until the day of Jesus Christ;
texts.php.1.7: According as it is right in me to have this regard in behalf of you all,—because ye have had me in your hearts, both in my bonds and in the defence and confirmation of the glad-message, all of you being, joint partakers of my favour.
texts.php.1.8: For God is, my witness, how I long for you all in the tender affections of Christ Jesus.
texts.php.1.9: And, this, I pray—that, your love, may be, yet more and more, pre-eminent in personal knowledge and all perception,
texts.php.1.10: To the end ye may be putting to the test the things that differ, in order that ye may be incorrupt and may give no occasion of stumbling, unto the day of Christ,
texts.php.1.11: Filled with that fruit of righteousness which is through Jesus Christ unto the glory and praise of God.
texts.php.1.12: Howbeit, I am minded, brethren, that ye should be, getting to know, that, the things which relate unto myself, rather, unto an advancement of the glad-message, have fallen out,
texts.php.1.13: So that, my bonds, have become manifest in Christ, in the whole palace, and unto all the rest,—
texts.php.1.14: And [so that], the most of the brethren in the Lord, assured by my bonds, are becoming more abundantly bold to be fearlessly speaking the word of God:—
texts.php.1.15: Some, indeed, by reason of envy and strife—some, however, by reason of good will—are proclaiming, the Christ:
texts.php.1.16: These, indeed, out of love, knowing that, for the defence of the glad-message, I am set;
texts.php.1.17: But, those, out of faction, are declaring, the Christ, not purely—supposing to rouse up, tribulation, with my bonds.
texts.php.1.18: What then? That, in any way, whether in pretext, or in truth, Christ, is declared, and, in this, I rejoice—yea, and will rejoice!
texts.php.1.19: For I know that, this, shall turn unto me for salvation—through your supplication, and the supply of the Spirit of Jesus Christ,—
texts.php.1.20: According to my eager outlook and hope, that, in nothing, shall I be put to shame, but, with all freedom of speech, as always, now also, shall Christ be magnified in my body, whether through means of life, or of death.
texts.php.1.21: For, unto me—living, is Christ, and, dying, gain.
texts.php.1.22: But, if living in flesh, [is Christ], this, unto me, is a fruit of work,—and, what I shall choose, I make not known:
texts.php.1.23: I am held in constraint, however, by reason of the two,—having, the coveting, to be released, and to be with, Christ, for it were far better!
texts.php.1.24: But, to abide still in the flesh, is more needful for your sake;
texts.php.1.25: And, of, this, being assured, know that I shall abide,—yea abide with you all, for your advancement, and the joy of your faith;
texts.php.1.26: In order that, your matter of boasting, may be more abundant in Christ Jesus, regarding me, through my own presence again with you.
texts.php.1.27: Only, in a manner worthy of the glad-message of the Christ, be using your citizenship; in order that—whether coming and seeing you, or being absent, I may hear of the things which concern you—that ye are standing fast in one spirit, with one soul, joining for the combat along with the faith of the glad-message;
texts.php.1.28: And not being affrighted in anything by the opposers,—the which, is, unto them, a token of destruction, although of your salvation, and this from God;
texts.php.1.29: Because, unto you, hath it been given as a favour, in behalf of Christ, not only, on him, to believe, but also, in his behalf, to suffer:—
texts.php.1.30: Having, the same contest, which ye have seen in me, and now hear to be in me.
texts.php.2.1: If there be, therefore, any encouragement in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of spirit, if any tender affections and compassions,
texts.php.2.2: Fill ye up my joy—that, the same thing, ye esteem, the same love, possessing, joined in soul, the one thing, esteeming,—
texts.php.2.3: Nothing by way of faction, nothing by way of vain-glory,—but, in lowliness of mind, accounting, one another, superior to yourselves,—
texts.php.2.4: Not, to your own things, severally looking, but, to the things of others, severally:—
texts.php.2.5: The same thing, esteem, in yourselves, which also, in Christ Jesus, [ye esteem],—
texts.php.2.6: Who, in form of God, subsisting, not, a thing to be seized, accounted the being equal with God,
texts.php.2.7: But, himself, emptied, taking, a servant’s form, coming to be, in men’s likeness;
texts.php.2.8: And, in fashion, being found, as a man, humbled himself, becoming obedient as far as death, yea, death upon a cross.
texts.php.2.9: Wherefore also, God, uplifted him far on high, and favoured him with the name which is above every name,—
texts.php.2.10: In order that, in the name of Jesus, every knee might bow—of beings in heaven, and on earth, and underground,—
texts.php.2.11: And, every tongue, might openly confess—that Jesus Christ is, Lord, unto the glory of God the Father.
texts.php.2.12: So, then, my beloved—even as ye have always obeyed, not [as] in my presence only, but, now, much more, in my absence, with fear and trembling, your own salvation, be working out;
texts.php.2.13: For it is, God, who energiseth within you, both the desiring and the energising, in behalf of his good pleasure.
texts.php.2.14: All things, be doing, apart from murmurings and disputings;
texts.php.2.15: In order that ye may become faultless and inviolate, children of God, blameless amidst a crooked and perverted generation, amongst whom ye appear as luminaries in the world,
texts.php.2.16: A word of light, holding forth,—as a matter of boasting unto me, for the day of Christ,—that, not in vain, I ran, nor, in vain, I toiled:—
texts.php.2.17: Nay! if I am even to be poured out as a drink-offering, upon the sacrifice and public ministry of your faith, I rejoice, yea rejoice together with you all,—
texts.php.2.18: For the same cause, moreover, do, ye also, rejoice, yea rejoice together with me.
texts.php.2.19: I am hoping, however, in the Lord Jesus—Timothy, shortly, to send unto you, in order that, I also, may be of cheerful soul, when I have ascertained the things that concern you.
texts.php.2.20: For, no one, have I, of equal soul, who, genuinely, as to the things that concern you, will be anxious;
texts.php.2.21: For, they all, their own things, do seek, not the things of Christ Jesus;
texts.php.2.22: But, of the proof of him, be taking note,—that, as child, with father, with me, hath he done service for the glad-message;
texts.php.2.23: Him, indeed, therefore, am I hoping to send—as soon as I can look off from the things that concern myself,—forthwith.
texts.php.2.24: I am assured, however, in the Lord,—that I, myself, shall shortly come.
texts.php.2.25: Needful, nevertheless have I accounted it—Epaphroditus, my brother and fellow worker and fellow soldier, but your apostle and public minister to my need, to send unto you;
texts.php.2.26: Since he hath been longing to see, you all, and hath been in great distress, because ye had heard he was sick;—
texts.php.2.27: And, in fact, he was sick, nigh unto death; but, God, had mercy on him,—and, not on him only, but, on me also, lest, sorrow upon sorrow, I should have.
texts.php.2.28: The more promptly, therefore, have I sent him, that, seeing him again, ye may rejoice, and, I, the less sorrowful, may be.
texts.php.2.29: Be giving him welcome, therefore, in the Lord, with all joy; and, such as he, in honour, be holding,—
texts.php.2.30: Because, for the sake of the work of the Lord, unto death, he drew nigh, running hazard with his life, that he might fill up your lack of the public service, towards me.
texts.php.3.1: For the rest, my brethren—rejoice in the Lord. To be writing, the same things, unto you, to me, is not irksome, while, for you, is safe:—
texts.php.3.2: Beware of the dogs, beware of mischievous workers, beware of the mutilation;
texts.php.3.3: For, we, are the circumcision, who in the Spirit of God, are doing divine service, and are boasting in Christ Jesus, and, not in flesh, having confidence,—
texts.php.3.4: Although, indeed, I, might have confidence even in flesh. If any other thinketh to have confidence in flesh, I, more:—
texts.php.3.5: Circumcised, the eighth day, of the race of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, a Hebrew of Hebrews,—regarding law, a Pharisee,
texts.php.3.6: Regarding zeal, persecuting the assembly, regarding the righteousness that is in law, having become blameless.
texts.php.3.7: But, whatever things, unto me, were gain, the same, have I accounted, for the Christ’s sake, loss;
texts.php.3.8: Yea, doubtless! and I account all things to be, loss, because of the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for the sake of whom, the loss, of all things, have I suffered, and do account them refuse, in order that, Christ, I may win,
texts.php.3.9: And be found in him—not having a righteousness of my own, that which is by law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is, of God, upon my faith,—
texts.php.3.10: To get to know him, and the power of his resurrection and fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed unto his death,—
texts.php.3.11: If by any means I may advance to the earlier resurrection, which is from among the dead:
texts.php.3.12: Not that I have, already, received, or have, already, reached perfection, but I am pressing on—if I may even lay hold of that for which I have also been laid hold of by Christ [Jesus]:—
texts.php.3.13: Brethren! I, as to myself, reckon that I have, not yet, laid hold; one thing, however,—the things behind, forgetting, and, unto the things before, eagerly reaching out,
texts.php.3.14: With the goal in view, I press on for the prize of the upward calling of God in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.3.15: As many, therefore, as are full-grown, let, this, be our resolve; and, if, somewhat differently, ye are resolved, this, also, shall, God, unto you reveal.
texts.php.3.16: Nevertheless, whereunto we have advanced, in the same rank, stepping along.
texts.php.3.17: Imitators together of me, become ye, brethren, and keep an eye on them who, thus, are walking,—even as ye have, us, for, an ensample.
texts.php.3.18: For, many, are walking—of whom I have often been telling you, and, now, even weeping, am telling,—the enemies of the cross of the Christ;
texts.php.3.19: Whose, end, is destruction, whose, God, is the belly, and [whose], glory, is in their shame, who, upon the earthly things, are resolved.
texts.php.3.20: For, our citizenship, in the heavens, hath its rise; wherefore, a Saviour also, do we ardently await,—The Lord Jesus Christ,—
texts.php.3.21: Who will transfigure our humbled body, into conformity with his glorified body, according to the energy wherewith he is able even to subdue, unto himself, all things.
texts.php.4.1: So then, my brethren, beloved and longed for, my joy and crown,—thus, stand fast in the Lord, beloved.
texts.php.4.2: Euodia, I exhort, and, Syntche, I exhort,—on the same thing, to be resolved in the Lord:—
texts.php.4.3: Yea! I request thee also, true yokefellow, be thou helping together with these women,—who, indeed, in the joyful message, have maintained the combat with me, along with Clement also, and the rest of my fellow-workers, whose names, are in the book of life.
texts.php.4.4: Rejoice in the Lord always: again, I will say—rejoice!
texts.php.4.5: Let, your considerateness, be known unto all men. The Lord, is near:—
texts.php.4.6: For nothing, be anxious, but, in everything, by your prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let, your petitions, be made known unto God;
texts.php.4.7: And, the peace of God, which riseth above every mind, shall guard your hearts and your thoughts, in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.4.8: For the rest, brethren, whatsoever things are true, whatsoever things are dignified, whatsoever things are righteous, whatsoever things are chaste, whatsoever things are lovely, whatsoever things are of good report,—if there be any virtue, and if any praise, the same, be taking into account;
texts.php.4.9: The things which ye have both learned, and accepted, and heard, and seen in me, the same, practise;—and, the God of peace, shall be with you.
texts.php.4.10: Howbeit I have been made to rejoice in the Lord greatly—that, now, at length, ye have flourished in your care for me,—although, indeed, ye were caring, but lacked opportunity.
texts.php.4.11: Not that, as to coming short, I am speaking, for, I, have learned, in whatsoever circumstances I am, to be, independent:
texts.php.4.12: I know [what it is] even to be kept low, and I know [what it is] to have more than enough,—in every way, and in all things, have I been let into the secret—both to be well fed, and to be hungering, both to have more than enough, and to be coming short:
texts.php.4.13: I have might, for all things, in him that empowereth me.
texts.php.4.14: Nevertheless, nobly, have ye done, in taking fellowship with me in my tribulation.
texts.php.4.15: Ye know, moreover, even ye, Philippians,—that, in the beginning of the glad-message, when I went forth from Macedonia, not, so much as one assembly, with me had fellowship—in the matter of giving and receiving—save, ye alone,—
texts.php.4.16: That, even in Thessalonica, both once and again, unto my need, ye sent:—
texts.php.4.17: Not that I seek after the gift, but I seek after the fruit that is to abound unto your account.
texts.php.4.18: But I have all things in full, and have more than enough, I am filled, having welcomed from Epaphroditus the things that came from you,—a fragrance of sweet smell, an acceptable sacrifice, well pleasing unto God.
texts.php.4.19: And, my God, will fill up your every need, according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.
texts.php.4.20: Now, unto our God and Father, be the glory—unto the ages of ages. Amen!
texts.php.4.21: Salute ye every saint in Christ Jesus. The brethren who are with me, salute you.
texts.php.4.22: All the saints salute you, but especially they who are of Caesar’s household.
texts.php.4.23: The favour of our Lord Jesus Christ, be with your spirit.

texts.php.1.1: Pablo y Timoteo, siervos de Jesucristo, a todos los santos en Cristo Jesús que están en Filipos, con los obispos y diáconos:
texts.php.1.2: Gracia y paz a vosotros de parte de Dios nuestro Padre y del Señor Jesucristo.
texts.php.1.3: Doy gracias a mi Dios cada vez que me acuerdo de vosotros,
texts.php.1.4: siempre en todas mis oraciones rogando con gozo por todos vosotros,
texts.php.1.5: por vuestra comunión en el evangelio, desde el primer día hasta ahora;
texts.php.1.6: estando persuadido de esto, que el que comenzó en vosotros la buena obra, la perfeccionará hasta el día de Jesucristo.
texts.php.1.7: Como me es justo sentir esto de todos vosotros, por cuanto os tengo en el corazón; y en mis prisiones, y en la defensa y confirmación del evangelio, todos vosotros sois participantes conmigo de la gracia.
texts.php.1.8: Porque Dios me es testigo de cómo os amo a todos vosotros con el entrañable amor de Jesucristo.
texts.php.1.9: Y esto pido en oración, que vuestro amor abunde aun más y más en ciencia y en todo conocimiento,
texts.php.1.10: para que aprobéis lo mejor, a fin de que seáis sinceros e irreprensibles para el día de Cristo,
texts.php.1.11: llenos de frutos de justicia que son por medio de Jesucristo, para gloria y alabanza de Dios.
texts.php.1.12: Quiero que sepáis, hermanos, que las cosas que me han sucedido, han redundado más bien para el progreso del evangelio,
texts.php.1.13: de tal manera que mis prisiones se han hecho patentes en Cristo en todo el pretorio, y a todos los demás.
texts.php.1.14: Y la mayoría de los hermanos, cobrando ánimo en el Señor con mis prisiones, se atreven mucho más a hablar la palabra sin temor.
texts.php.1.15: Algunos, a la verdad, predican a Cristo por envidia y contienda; pero otros de buena voluntad.
texts.php.1.16: Los unos anuncian a Cristo por contención, no sinceramente, pensando añadir aflicción a mis prisiones;
texts.php.1.17: pero los otros por amor, sabiendo que estoy puesto para la defensa del evangelio.
texts.php.1.18: ¿Qué, pues? Que no obstante, de todas maneras, o por pretexto o por verdad, Cristo es anunciado; y en esto me gozo, y me gozaré aún.
texts.php.1.19: Porque sé que por vuestra oración y la suministración del Espíritu de Jesucristo, esto resultará en mi liberación,
texts.php.1.20: conforme a mi anhelo y esperanza de que en nada seré avergonzado; antes bien con toda confianza, como siempre, ahora también será magnificado Cristo en mi cuerpo, o por vida o por muerte.
texts.php.1.21: Porque para mí el vivir es Cristo, y el morir es ganancia.
texts.php.1.22: Mas si el vivir en la carne resulta para mí en beneficio de la obra, no sé entonces qué escoger.
texts.php.1.23: Porque de ambas cosas estoy puesto en estrecho, teniendo deseo de partir y estar con Cristo, lo cual es muchísimo mejor;
texts.php.1.24: pero quedar en la carne es más necesario por causa de vosotros.
texts.php.1.25: Y confiado en esto, sé que quedaré, que aún permaneceré con todos vosotros, para vuestro provecho y gozo de la fe,
texts.php.1.26: para que abunde vuestra gloria de mí en Cristo Jesús por mi presencia otra vez entre vosotros.
texts.php.1.27: Solamente que os comportéis como es digno del evangelio de Cristo, para que o sea que vaya a veros, o que esté ausente, oiga de vosotros que estáis firmes en un mismo espíritu, combatiendo unánimes por la fe del evangelio,
texts.php.1.28: y en nada intimidados por los que se oponen, que para ellos ciertamente es indicio de perdición, mas para vosotros de salvación, y esto de Dios.
texts.php.1.29: Porque a vosotros os es concedido a causa de Cristo, no solo que creáis en él, sino también que padezcáis por él,
texts.php.1.30: teniendo el mismo conflicto que habéis visto en mí, y ahora oís que hay en mí.
texts.php.2.1: Por tanto, si hay alguna consolación en Cristo, si algún consuelo de amor, si alguna comunión del Espíritu, si algún afecto entrañable, si alguna misericordia,
texts.php.2.2: completad mi gozo, sintiendo lo mismo, teniendo el mismo amor, unánimes, sintiendo una misma cosa.
texts.php.2.3: Nada hagáis por contienda o por vanagloria; antes bien con humildad, estimando cada uno a los demás como superiores a él mismo;
texts.php.2.4: no mirando cada uno por lo suyo propio, sino cada cual también por lo de los otros.
texts.php.2.5: Haya, pues, en vosotros este sentir que hubo también en Cristo Jesús,
texts.php.2.6: el cual, siendo en forma de Dios, no estimó el ser igual a Dios como cosa a que aferrarse,
texts.php.2.7: sino que se despojó a sí mismo, tomando forma de siervo, hecho semejante a los hombres;
texts.php.2.8: y estando en la condición de hombre, se humilló a sí mismo, haciéndose obediente hasta la muerte, y muerte de cruz.
texts.php.2.9: Por lo cual Dios también le exaltó hasta lo sumo, y le dio un nombre que es sobre todo nombre,
texts.php.2.10: para que en el nombre de Jesús se doble toda rodilla de los que están en los cielos, y en la tierra, y debajo de la tierra;
texts.php.2.11: y toda lengua confiese que Jesucristo es el Señor, para gloria de Dios Padre.
texts.php.2.12: Por tanto, amados míos, como siempre habéis obedecido, no como en mi presencia solamente, sino mucho más ahora en mi ausencia, ocupaos en vuestra salvación con temor y temblor,
texts.php.2.13: porque Dios es el que en vosotros produce así el querer como el hacer, por su buena voluntad.
texts.php.2.14: Haced todo sin murmuraciones y contiendas,
texts.php.2.15: para que seáis irreprensibles y sencillos, hijos de Dios sin mancha en medio de una generación maligna y perversa, en medio de la cual resplandecéis como luminares en el mundo;
texts.php.2.16: asidos de la palabra de vida, para que en el día de Cristo yo pueda gloriarme de que no he corrido en vano, ni en vano he trabajado.
texts.php.2.17: Y aunque sea derramado en libación sobre el sacrificio y servicio de vuestra fe, me gozo y regocijo con todos vosotros.
texts.php.2.18: Y asimismo gozaos y regocijaos también vosotros conmigo.
texts.php.2.19: Espero en el Señor Jesús enviaros pronto a Timoteo, para que yo también esté de buen ánimo al saber de vuestro estado;
texts.php.2.20: pues a ninguno tengo del mismo ánimo, y que tan sinceramente se interese por vosotros.
texts.php.2.21: Porque todos buscan lo suyo propio, no lo que es de Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.2.22: Pero ya conocéis los méritos de él, que como hijo a padre ha servido conmigo en el evangelio.
texts.php.2.23: Así que a este espero enviaros, luego que yo vea cómo van mis asuntos;
texts.php.2.24: y confío en el Señor que yo también iré pronto a vosotros.
texts.php.2.25: Mas tuve por necesario enviaros a Epafrodito, mi hermano y colaborador y compañero de milicia, vuestro mensajero, y ministrador de mis necesidades;
texts.php.2.26: porque él tenía gran deseo de veros a todos vosotros, y gravemente se angustió porque habíais oído que había enfermado.
texts.php.2.27: Pues en verdad estuvo enfermo, a punto de morir; pero Dios tuvo misericordia de él, y no solamente de él, sino también de mí, para que yo no tuviese tristeza sobre tristeza.
texts.php.2.28: Así que le envío con mayor prontitud, para que al verle de nuevo os gocéis, y yo esté con menos tristeza.
texts.php.2.29: Recibidle, pues, en el Señor, con todo gozo, y tened en estima a los que son como él;
texts.php.2.30: porque por la obra de Cristo estuvo próximo a la muerte, exponiendo su vida para suplir lo que faltaba en vuestro servicio por mí.
texts.php.3.1: Por lo demás, hermanos míos, gozaos en el Señor. A mí no me es molesto el escribiros las mismas cosas, y para vosotros es seguro.
texts.php.3.2: Guardaos de los perros, guardaos de los malos obreros, guardaos de los mutiladores del cuerpo.
texts.php.3.3: Porque nosotros somos la circuncisión, los que en espíritu servimos a Dios y nos gloriamos en Cristo Jesús, no teniendo confianza en la carne.
texts.php.3.4: Aunque yo tengo también de qué confiar en la carne. Si alguno piensa que tiene de qué confiar en la carne, yo más:
texts.php.3.5: circuncidado al octavo día, del linaje de Israel, de la tribu de Benjamín, hebreo de hebreos; en cuanto a la ley, fariseo;
texts.php.3.6: en cuanto a celo, perseguidor de la iglesia; en cuanto a la justicia que es en la ley, irreprensible.
texts.php.3.7: Pero cuantas cosas eran para mí ganancia, las he estimado como pérdida por amor de Cristo.
texts.php.3.8: Y ciertamente, aun estimo todas las cosas como pérdida por la excelencia del conocimiento de Cristo Jesús, mi Señor, por amor del cual lo he perdido todo, y lo tengo por basura, para ganar a Cristo,
texts.php.3.9: y ser hallado en él, no teniendo mi propia justicia, que es por la ley, sino la que es por la fe de Cristo, la justicia que es de Dios por la fe;
texts.php.3.10: a fin de conocerle, y el poder de su resurrección, y la participación de sus padecimientos, llegando a ser semejante a él en su muerte,
texts.php.3.11: si en alguna manera llegase a la resurrección de entre los muertos.
texts.php.3.12: No que lo haya alcanzado ya, ni que ya sea perfecto; sino que prosigo, por ver si logro asir aquello para lo cual fui también asido por Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.3.13: Hermanos, yo mismo no pretendo haberlo ya alcanzado; pero una cosa hago: olvidando ciertamente lo que queda atrás, y extendiéndome a lo que está delante,
texts.php.3.14: prosigo a la meta, al premio del supremo llamamiento de Dios en Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.3.15: Así que, todos los que somos perfectos, esto mismo sintamos; y si otra cosa sentís, esto también os lo revelará Dios.
texts.php.3.16: Pero en aquello a que hemos llegado, sigamos una misma regla, sintamos una misma cosa.
texts.php.3.17: Hermanos, sed imitadores de mí, y mirad a los que así se conducen según el ejemplo que tenéis en nosotros.
texts.php.3.18: Porque por ahí andan muchos, de los cuales os dije muchas veces, y aun ahora lo digo llorando, que son enemigos de la cruz de Cristo;
texts.php.3.19: el fin de los cuales será perdición, cuyo dios es el vientre, y cuya gloria es su vergüenza; que solo piensan en lo terrenal.
texts.php.3.20: Mas nuestra ciudadanía está en los cielos, de donde también esperamos al Salvador, al Señor Jesucristo;
texts.php.3.21: el cual transformará el cuerpo de la humillación nuestra, para que sea semejante al cuerpo de la gloria suya, por el poder con el cual puede también sujetar a sí mismo todas las cosas.
texts.php.4.1: Así que, hermanos míos amados y deseados, gozo y corona mía, estad así firmes en el Señor, amados.
texts.php.4.2: Ruego a Evodia y a Síntique, que sean de un mismo sentir en el Señor.
texts.php.4.3: Asimismo te ruego también a ti, compañero fiel, que ayudes a estas que combatieron juntamente conmigo en el evangelio, con Clemente también y los demás colaboradores míos, cuyos nombres están en el libro de la vida.
texts.php.4.4: Regocijaos en el Señor siempre. Otra vez digo: ¡Regocijaos!
texts.php.4.5: Vuestra gentileza sea conocida de todos los hombres. El Señor está cerca.
texts.php.4.6: Por nada estéis afanosos, sino sean conocidas vuestras peticiones delante de Dios en toda oración y ruego, con acción de gracias.
texts.php.4.7: Y la paz de Dios, que sobrepasa todo entendimiento, guardará vuestros corazones y vuestros pensamientos en Cristo Jesús.
texts.php.4.8: Por lo demás, hermanos, todo lo que es verdadero, todo lo honesto, todo lo justo, todo lo puro, todo lo amable, todo lo que es de buen nombre; si hay virtud alguna, si algo digno de alabanza, en esto pensad.
texts.php.4.9: Lo que aprendisteis y recibisteis y oísteis y visteis en mí, esto haced; y el Dios de paz estará con vosotros.
texts.php.4.10: En gran manera me gocé en el Señor de que ya al fin habéis revivido vuestro cuidado de mí; de lo cual también estabais solícitos, pero os faltaba la oportunidad.
texts.php.4.11: No lo digo porque tenga escasez, pues he aprendido a contentarme, cualquiera que sea mi situación.
texts.php.4.12: Sé vivir humildemente, y sé tener abundancia; en todo y por todo estoy enseñado, así para estar saciado como para tener hambre, así para tener abundancia como para padecer necesidad.
texts.php.4.13: Todo lo puedo en Cristo que me fortalece.
texts.php.4.14: Sin embargo, bien hicisteis en participar conmigo en mi tribulación.
texts.php.4.15: Y sabéis también vosotros, oh filipenses, que al principio de la predicación del evangelio, cuando partí de Macedonia, ninguna iglesia participó conmigo en razón de dar y recibir, sino vosotros solos;
texts.php.4.16: pues aun a Tesalónica me enviasteis una y otra vez para mis necesidades.
texts.php.4.17: No es que busque dádivas, sino que busco fruto que abunde en vuestra cuenta.
texts.php.4.18: Pero todo lo he recibido, y tengo abundancia; estoy lleno, habiendo recibido de Epafrodito lo que enviasteis; olor fragante, sacrificio acepto, agradable a Dios.
